8601.full: the goat-stag , as the Greeks called a fantastic animal, represented on Eastern carpets and the like, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8608.full: 1. thirty years old , (Plato Philosophus); in contracted form, οἱ τριακοντοῦται the men of thirty years , (Plato Philosophus); feminine τριακοντοῦτις (Isaeus Orator) 2. τριακονταέτης, ες, of or for thirty years , (Thucydides);—;in feminine form, σπονδαὶ τριηκοντουτίδες (Herdotus Historicus); αἱ τριακοντούτιδες σπονδαί (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8610.full: the third wave, a huge wave , for the third was supposed to be the largest (as in Lat. the fluctus decumanus) , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, τρ. κακῶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

8613.full: 1. thrice as many, thrice as much, thrice as great as , with genitive, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: —;absolute, τριπλασίαν δύναμιν εἶχε (i.e. τῆς προτέρας); (Xenophon Historicus) 2. τριπλάσιον as adverb, τριπλάσιον thrice as much , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8617.full: 1. to tremble, quake, quiver , especially from fear, (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive to fear to do, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. with accusative to tremble before or at a person, to stand in awe of , (Homer) In each sense (Homer) uses both Act. and Mid., but only in present and imperfect; epic and ionic τρομεοίατο for τρομέοιντο, (Iliad by Homer); ionic participle τρομεύμενος (Solon Lyricus) (ML)

8629.full: 1. to make knobby :—;Pass., ῥόπαλα σιδήρῳ τετυλωμένα clubs knobbed with iron, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to make callous , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be callous , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

s: to torture by beating, beat to death
8631.full: τυμπανίζω (τύμπανον, a kettle-drum), [in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (17 pi?) * ;] __1. to beat a drum. __2. to torture by beating, beat to death (cf. Westc. on He, l.with): pass., Heb.11:35.† (AS)

8633.lxx: in LXX: Isa.42:19 (עִוֵּר), Tob.7:7 א, Wis.2:21 א *
8633.full: τυφλόω, -ῶ (τυφλός), [in LXX: Isa.42:19 (עִוֵּר), Tob.7:7 א, Wis.2:21 א * ;] to blind, make blind: metaphorically, Jhn.12:40 (LXX, καμμύω), 2Co.4:4, 1Jn.2:11.† (AS)

8634.full: a ditch, trench , (Homer), etc.; τάφρον ὀρύσσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τ. ἐλαύνειν to draw a trench , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

8636.lxx: in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) *
8636.full: τίλλω [in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) * ;] to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας, Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.† (AS)

s: an estimate of damages, a penalty
8637.full: 1. an estimate, valuation , (Euripides) 2. an estimate of damages, a penalty , Lat. litis aestimatio, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;generally a payment , τύμβου for neglect of his tomb, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. estimate of property for taxation, rateable property , Lat. census, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ τιμημάτων πολιτεία, = τιμοκρατία, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: to make visible, clear, manifest or known
8643.full: φανερόω, -ώ [in LXX: Jer.40:6 (33:6) (גָּלָה pi.) * ;] to make visible, clear, manifest or known: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.2:11 17:6, Rom.1:19, 1Co.4:5, 2Co.2:14 11:6, Col.4:4, Tit.1:3; pass., Mrk.4:22, Jhn.3:21 9:3, Rom.3:21 16:26, 2Co.4:10-11, Eph.5:13, Col.1:26, 2Ti.1:10, Heb.9:8, 1Jn.3:2 Jn 4:9, Rev.3:18 15:4; with accusative of person(s), of Christ, Jhn.7:4 21:1; pass., 2Co.3:3 5:10-11, 1Jn.2:19; of Christ, Mrk.16:12, 14, Jhn.1:31 21:14, Col.3:4, 1Ti.3:16, Heb.9:26, 1Pe.1:20 5:4, 1Jn.1:2 (ἡ ζωή; see Westc., in l) 1Jn.2:28 Jn 3:2 Jn 3:5 Jn 3:8.† SYN.: see: ἀποκαλύπτω (AS)

8644.full: φανερῶς adv. (φανερός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:28 * ;] __(a) manifestly, openly: Mrk.1:45; opposite to ἐν κρυπτῷ„ Jhn.7:10; __(b) clearly: Act.10:3 (2Ma.3:28).† (AS)

8646.full: φανός, -οῦ, ὁ (φαίνω), a torch or lantern (see Rutherford, NPhr., 131 f.): Jhn.18:3.† SYN.: see: λαμπάς (AS)

8660.full: φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 2:15 א1 * ;] love of money, avarice: 1Ti.6:1.† SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv) (AS)

8661.full: love of rule, lust of power , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

s: to be so obstinate as to choose
8666.full: 1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose the worst, (Thucydides) 2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

s: to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous
8670.full: φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:35 A ;] to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): with inf., Rom.15:20, 2Co.5:9, 1Th.4:11.† (AS)

s: loving that which is good, loving goodness
8672.full: φιλ-άγαθος, -ον [in LXX: Wis.7:22 * ;] loving that which is good, loving goodness: Tit.1:8 (Arist., Polyb., a l.).† (AS)

8674.full: φιλό-νεικος, -ον (νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Eze.3:7 (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;] fond of strife, contentious: 1Co.11:16.† (AS)

8676.lxx: in LXX: Deu.25:4 (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R *
8676.full: φιμόω, -ῶ (φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: Deu.25:4 (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R * ;] to muzzle: 1Co.9:9, 1Ti.5:18" (LXX) ; metaphorically, to put to silence: with accusative of person(s), Mat.22:34, 1Pe.2:15; pass., to be silenced, silent: Mat.22:12, Mrk.1:25 4:39, Luk.4:35.† (AS)

8679.full: 1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a vein of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8681.full: φλύαρος, -ον (φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;] babbling, garrulous: 1Ti.5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, 4Mac, l.with).† (AS)

8684.full: purple-red, purple or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus, (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8686.full: φονεύς, -έως, ὁ (φόνος) [in LXX: Wis.12:5 * ;] a murderer: Mat.22:7 Act.7:52 28:4, 1Pe.4:15, Rev.21:8 22:15; ἀνὴρ φ., Act.3:14.† SYN.: ἀνθρωποκτόνος (AS)

8690.full: φορτίζω (φόρτος), [in LXX: Eze.16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;] to load: with dupl. accusative, Luk.11:46; pass., to be laden: metaphorically (EV, heavy laden), Mat.11:28.† (AS)

8692.full: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—;neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

8696.full: φύλαξ, -ακος, ὁ (φυλάσσω), [in LXX for שָׁמַר, צוּר ;] a guard, keeper: Act.5:23 12:6, 19.† (AS)
